tool.name: 3DTrees: SmartTile
tool.description: Tile, filter, merge and remap point clouds

collection.name: @NAME@
collection.label: ${tool.name}: Output @RES@ (${'Original resolution' if $operation.tile_outputs[@RES@-1].resolution.mode == 'original' else str($operation.tile_outputs[@RES@-1].resolution.resolution_cm) + ' cm'})${' — ' + str($operation.instances.instance_dimension).split(',')[@DIM@-1].strip() if $operation.instances.mode == 'whole' else ''}
collection.filter: operation['task'] == 'tile' and len(operation['tile_outputs']) >= @RES@ and (@DIM@ == 1 or (operation['instances']['mode'] == 'whole' and len(operation['instances']['instance_dimension'].split(',')) >= @DIM@))

param.name: resolution_1_cm
param.label: Prediction voxel size (cm)
param.help: Voxel size of the prediction files supplied above. Use 1 cm after transfer to 1 cm tiles, or 10 cm for direct 10 cm predictions. Matching radius is the voxel diagonal; original output points are retained.

param.name: mode
param.label: Merged resolution
param.help: Subsampled keeps one original point per voxel; full resolution keeps every input point in record order (for example as input to ForestStructure).

param.name: merged_resolution_cm
param.label: Merged resolution (cm)
param.help: Target spacing for merged files, 1–100 cm.

param.label: Add OriginalPointIndex
param.help: Numbers every point by its record position across the input files (sorted by name), as the first ExtraByte (uint64 in LAZ/COPC; uint32 in full-resolution PLY, with an error on overflow). ForestStructure uses it to restore source record order after COPC reorders points.

param.label: Merged formats
param.help: Select one or more output encodings for merged files.

param.name: input_files
param.label: Input LAZ/LAS files
param.help: One or more source point clouds to tile and subsample.

param.name: mode
param.label: Tiling mode
param.option: Buffered spatial tiles for downstream processing
Keep existing instances whole for species prediction

param.label: Subsampling method
param.help: Point kept for each voxel: center of mass is the mean of the original points in the voxel; nearest to centroid is the original point closest to that mean.

param.name: instance_dimension
param.label: Instance dimensions
param.help: Comma-separated tree ID fields, up to six. Example: PredInstance_SAT,PredInstance_FM. Each field produces a separate collection at every selected resolution.

validator.message: Use up to six comma-separated dimension names, each starting with a letter or underscore.
Specify each instance dimension only once.

param.validator: len([d.strip() for d in value.split(',')]) == len(set(d.strip() for d in value.split(',')))

param.name: attributes
param.label: Additional attributes to retain
param.help: Comma-separated fields, such as intensity. The instance field is always retained.

param.label: Tile length (m)
param.help: Target tile edge length in meters.

param.label: Tile buffer (m)
param.help: Overlap added around each tile in meters. The tile grid always starts at the south-west corner of the data extent.

param.label: Tiling threshold (MB)
param.help: Skip tiling for a single input below this size and still create normalized subsampled outputs.

repeat.name: tile_outputs
repeat.title: Output
repeat.help: One collection per resolution; in whole-instance mode, one per resolution and instance dimension. Original resolution keeps every point.

param.name: resolution_cm
param.label: Voxel size (cm)
param.help: Typically 10 cm for segmentation or 1 cm for fine detail. Whole-instance mode samples each tree separately.

param.name: format
param.label: Format
param.help: LAZ and COPC LAZ support the remap workflow. PLY is binary; whole-instance outputs retain the tree ID and selected attributes.

param.name: input_segmented
param.label: Segmented tiles
param.help: Segmented tiles from one SmartTile run, with independent tile-local instance IDs. Segmentation must preserve their coordinates.

param.name: segmented_resolution_cm
param.label: Voxel size (cm)
param.help: Voxel size used to prepare these segmented tiles. With high-resolution targets, the transfer radius is the voxel diagonal: 10 cm gives 17.32 cm.

param.name: type
param.label: Model
param.help: The model that produced the segmented files.
param.option: SegmentAnyTree, ForestMamba or other point predictions

param.label: Instance dimension
param.help: Name of the prediction instance dimension in the segmented files, for example PredInstance_SAT or PredInstance_FM.

validator.message: Use letters, numbers, and underscores only; start with a letter or underscore.

param.name: input_tree_files
param.label: Tree tables from 3dtrees_raycloudtools
param.help: Both the *_trees.txt and *_trees_info.txt table for every segmented tile; required to keep whole trees and their tree IDs.

param.name: input_tree_meshes
param.label: QSM tree meshes from 3dtrees_raycloudtools
param.help: Optional: the *_trees_mesh.ply of every segmented tile (RayCloudTools 1.3.0 or newer, with per-face tree IDs). Filtered with the same IDs as the tiles and tables.

param.name: tile_bounds_json
param.label: Tile bounds JSON
param.help: Tile bounds JSON emitted by the tile task for the same tiling run.

param.name: input_res1
param.label: High-resolution tiles
param.help: Finer tiles from the same SmartTile run. Leave empty to filter the segmented tiles at their existing resolution.

param.name: resolution_1_cm
param.label: Voxel size (cm)
param.help: Voxel size of these target tiles, usually 1 cm. Recorded as the processed prediction resolution. Ignored when no target tiles are supplied.

param.label: Ownership anchor
param.help: Point of each instance whose XY position decides which tile core owns it; the centroid is the XY centroid.

param.name: enabled
param.label: Cross-tile instance reconciliation
param.help: Reconcile overlapping predictions of the same tree across tiles. Input IDs are always treated as independent within each tile; disabling reconciliation keeps those instances separate. RayCloudTools retains its table-linked tile identities.

param.label: Overlap threshold
param.help: Minimum shared-point ratio for reconciling instances across tiles, above 0 and at most 1.

validator.message: The overlap threshold must be above 0 and at most 1.

param.name: enabled
param.label: Small cluster reassignment
param.help: After deduplication, give small instances the ID of the remaining instance with the nearest XY centroid (horizontal distance, within 5 m). Not available for RayCloudTools.

param.label: Max bounding-box volume (m3)
param.help: Instances below this axis-aligned bounding-box volume are small.

param.label: Max cluster size (points)
param.help: Only instances with fewer points in the processed tiles are checked against the volume limit.

param.name: merged_file
param.label: Merged LAZ/COPC LAZ file
param.help: Single merged prediction file whose extra dimensions should be transferred to originals.

param.name: merged_file_is_copc
param.label: Merged file is COPC LAZ
param.help: Preserve the .copc.laz suffix for tools that infer COPC status from the file name.

param.name: collection
param.label: Segmented files collection
param.help: Prediction tiles for one model, including whole-instance outputs after species prediction.

param.name: type
param.label: Model
param.help: RayCloudTools collections also need the filtered tree tables from the merge task.
param.option: SegmentAnyTree, ForestMamba or other point predictions

param.name: tree_files
param.label: RayCloudTools tree tables
param.help: The filtered *_trees.txt and *_trees_info.txt tables emitted by the merge task.

param.name: tree_meshes
param.label: RayCloudTools QSM tree meshes
param.help: Optional: the filtered tree meshes emitted by the merge task.

param.label: Dimension allowlist
param.help: Comma-separated extra dimensions to transfer; empty transfers all extra dimensions.

validator.message: Use comma-separated dimension names containing only letters, numbers, and underscores.

param.label: Instance dimension
param.help: For a custom tree ID field, enter the same name used for whole-instance tiling (for example CustomTreeId). PredInstance-prefixed fields and treeID are also recognized automatically. A custom field name applies to every prediction collection in this run.

validator.message: Use a dimension name starting with a letter or underscore.

param.label: Match within the same existing instance
param.help: For species predictions from whole-instance tiles: originals and predictions must contain the same instance field selected above. Copy attributes only from the same tree and preserve its ID.

param.name: original_files
param.label: Original LAZ/LAS files
param.help: Original uploaded files to enrich with remapped prediction dimensions.

param.name: mode
param.label: Resolution of supplied predictions
param.help: Controls matching distance, not output density. Choose the current resolution of the prediction files above. Original resolution means predictions retain original points and are matched within coordinate precision.

repeat.name: original_collections
repeat.title: Original collection
repeat.help: Add one collection per version of the same originals, for example SAT predictions first and ForestMamba predictions second. Matching filenames and point order are required; shared attributes must agree.

param.name: files
param.label: Original files with predictions
param.help: Select a collection or files. Each entry must contain the same originals; their prediction attributes are combined into one merged file.

param.label: Output formats
param.help: Select one or more formats for the merged file.

tool.help:
**SmartTile 2.4 workflows**
For original-resolution prediction tiles, choose **Resolution of supplied predictions → Original resolution** in Remap. This mode requires full coverage for every model, including RCT; unmatched points fail instead of becoming background. Coordinates are matched within LAS encoding precision, including after COPC reordering; every original point still requires a match. Enable **Match within the same existing instance** for species predictions.
1. Original → Tile → SegmentAnyTree/ForestMamba → Filter/Merge → species prediction → Remap → visualization. Create fine (typically 1 cm) and coarse (10 cm) spatial tiles. Filter/Merge transfers coarse predictions to the fine geometry and resolves overlaps using the matching tile bounds JSON. Give Remap each model's final prediction collection and the originals. 2. Original with predictions → whole-instance Tile → species prediction → same-instance Remap → visualization. Choose "Keep existing instances whole", enter one or more existing ID fields and add entries under Output. Choose a voxel size or Original resolution to keep every point. Each field is tiled independently: every tree stays in exactly one tile for that field, and its ID is always retained. These tiles need no separate filter. For already-dense buffered prediction tiles, choose Filter / merge and leave High-resolution tiles empty, using their original tile bounds JSON before species prediction. Plain spatial tiles contain geometry, not existing tree IDs. 3. Multiple segmentation attribute versions → Create merged file → full-resolution COPC → ForestStructure. Add an **Original collection** entry for each version of the same originals, for example originals with SAT predictions, then the same originals with ForestMamba predictions. Each entry accepts a collection or a list of files. Filenames and point order must agree across entries; shared fields must contain equal values. Choose full resolution, COPC LAZ and "Add OriginalPointIndex".
**Tiling and filtering**
Inputs must share a projected CRS in metres, or all have no CRS and use local metres. Reproject degree, geocentric or foot-based inputs first. Spatial tiles use buffered cores; the Output entries control their resolution and format. Both tiling modes use the same Output selections and formats. Whole-instance outputs retain XYZ, the required instance field and selected additional attributes. Original resolution keeps duplicate points as well as unique coordinates. IDs must already be globally meaningful across the input files.
For example, enter ``PredInstance_SAT,PredInstance_FM`` under **Instance dimensions** and request Original resolution plus 10 cm: Galaxy returns four separate tile collections, one for each dimension and resolution. Collections follow dimension order, then Output entry order. Each collection retains its own instance field and the selected additional attributes. The wrapper accepts up to six instance dimensions and six Output entries.
Filter / merge accepts segmented tiles and optional high-resolution targets. With targets, predictions are transferred onto their geometry using a radius calculated as sqrt(3) times the segmented input voxel size (10 cm gives about 17.32 cm). Without targets, prediction transfer is skipped and the supplied geometry is filtered directly. Both apply ownership, recovery, reconciliation and duplicate removal and use the same processed tiles output. Inputs must come from one SmartTile run, and segmentation must preserve coordinates. Instance IDs are treated independently within each tile. Ownership, cross-tile reconciliation and small-cluster reassignment are under Advanced options. Disabling reconciliation keeps tile instances separate; small-cluster reassignment changes IDs only and is disabled by default. The processed resolution is the target voxel size when targets are supplied, otherwise the segmented input voxel size.
RayCloudTools merge/remap requires both tree tables for every tile. Optional QSM meshes must carry per-face tree IDs. Tables and meshes follow the same retained IDs. For RCT, choose its RayCloudTools model and supply both tree tables. High-resolution targets are optional for RCT as well. Filter / merge returns processed tiles and the applicable RCT companions. Use Remap to enrich originals and Create merged file to build a combined product.
**Remapping**
In subsampled mode, every non-RCT collection must cover 100% of the original points within the fine-resolution voxel diagonal (17.32 mm at 1 cm). Set the resolution to match the supplied predictions. RCT points without a surviving tree become background zero. Same-instance remap copies attributes only from the matching existing tree and keeps original IDs; use it for whole-instance species outputs. Set Instance dimension to the field used for whole-instance tiling when its name is custom (for example CustomTreeId); originals and predictions must both carry that field. The default PredInstance also recognizes PredInstance-prefixed fields and treeID automatically. Use separate remap runs for collections with different custom field names. Equal-distance choices are deterministic across worker and batch counts.
**Products and metadata**
Subsampled products retain an original point nearest each voxel mean. Full-resolution products retain every point and normally add a source-order index as the first ExtraByte. LAZ/COPC stores this index as uint64; full-resolution PLY stores uint32 and fails if an index or total count exceeds 4,294,967,295. Disabling index generation preserves an existing field. ForestStructure needs full-resolution COPC with the index enabled.
LAZ/COPC preserve compatible CRS, attributes and missing-value declarations; incompatible source schemas fail explicitly. PLY is binary and carries CRS as a comment, but cannot represent LAS missing-value declarations or general 64-bit integer fields. COPC is returned to Galaxy with the LAZ datatype. Inputs are linked into the job directory under their dataset names and are never modified; duplicate names fail before processing.
CPU usage follows Galaxy's allocation. Dense cells can exceed the tiler's point-count target; the scheduler/container enforces the job RAM limit. Large jobs also need scratch disk. This wrapper does not change the server's resource allocation.
